propositions: At search exhaustion, fallback-banked criterion verdicts incorrectly bank `met=false` (evidence-of-absence as refutation) instead of distinguishing exhaustion via `evidence_sufficient:false` marker, causing false FAIL verdicts on tickets whose evidence exists but was not found within budget.

The banking write path must widen the `fallback_record` contract to accept and persist an optional `evidence_sufficient:false` marker alongside bool `met`, preserved on overwrite by `harvest_structured_into_bank` and re-stamped authoritative-from-bank by `merge_finalizer_with_bank`, keeping the model-facing tool bool-only.

`record_criterion_verdict` stays bool-only; bare `met=false` signals positive refutation; not-found records nothing; only the bounded fallback at the COMMIT boundary calls new `record_insufficient(source='fallback')` to bank exhaustion-marked verdicts.

Schema, renderers (`_render_verdict_text`, close_precheck), `reconcile_verdict` (derives top-level marker + marker-aware remediation), and sidecar FAIL payload must key on the `evidence_sufficient` marker to distinguish insufficient from unmet, honoring fail-closed (FAIL verdict unchanged) but messaging exhaustion as re-verify + evidence-discovery, not unmet-criteria guidance.

Audit-page verdict consumer was a shape-based PASS/FAIL discriminator (`'criteria' in sidecar`) that broke when FAIL payload gained criteria for marker round-trip; fixed by keying on verdict value instead, enabling per-criterion markers in FAIL records.

Extraction of verdict-assembly functions (`assemble_deterministic_verdict`, `merge_finalizer_with_bank`) into `completion_verdict_assembly.py` (258 LOC) preserved completion_banking.py under 800-LOC cap while re-exporting to callers unchanged.
